public_rationale: On the ordinary capability reading, both parts hold. Stanford demonstrated instruction-directed generation at substantial scale, and the DIPPER experiments showed that automated paraphrasing reduced detection while preserving meaning. This supports suitability and adaptability, not literal perfection. The same detector study demonstrated an effective retrieval defense, so the evidence does not support an interpretation that every detector can always be defeated.
limitations: The result depends on reading perfect as rhetorical suitability.
Text-classifier evasion does not establish reliable manipulation of arbitrary recommendation algorithms.
The selected calendar-year window is an interpretation of an undated ongoing capability claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI is a perfect tool for soullessly churning out content to match a set of instructions such as an algorithm's, and while an algorithm can theoretically be tuned to evaluate content as human, scaled content can likewise be tweaked to seem more human.

statement.excerpt: Generative AI is a perfect tool for soullessly churning out content to match a particular set of instructions — such as those that an algorithm follows — and while an algorithm can theoretically be tuned to evaluate content as "human," so can scaled content be tweaked to make it seem more human.

our_interpretation: Read perfect tool as strong suitability for repeatable instruction-directed generation, rather than literal error-free performance.
Read seem more human as increasing the likelihood that an automated human-versus-machine classifier accepts generated text as human-written.

The claim describes an existing capability without a reporting period. Use 2023, the latest completed calendar year before the post, for contemporary empirical capability evidence; such research has no standard quarterly reporting cycle.
Theoretical detector tuning is explanatory language, not an antecedent requiring a future event.
The claim does not require defeating every detector or reverse-engineering every platform's ranking system.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary demonstrations establish large-scale instruction-directed generation, and controlled evaluations show that modifying generated content materially reduces detection while preserving useful content.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary systematic evidence establishes that usable instruction-directed generation cannot be repeated at scale, or that the proposed modifications do not make generated content more likely to pass credible human-content classifiers.

evidence.publisher: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models
evidence.explanation: The researchers generated tens of thousands of instruction-following examples, establishing repeatable production at scale. Their accompanying evaluation and limitations do not establish flawless adherence or universal content quality.

Controlled evaluations show that automated rewriting can make generated text substantially harder to identify without simply destroying its meaning. This directly supports the classifier-evasion reading.

evidence.locator: Section 5.3, Is retrieval an effective detector with a large retrieval corpus?
evidence.explanation: The same paper demonstrates a defense that compares candidate text against stored model outputs. It limits any stronger interpretation that modification makes detection impossible, but does not negate the demonstrated ability to evade other detectors.
